name: Pediatric medial minimally invasive approach to the distal tibia
corridor: Short medial distal incision with submuscular/epiperiosteal plate advancement proximally while preserving physis and perichondral ring

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with medial distal tibia accessible and full-length AP/lateral imaging available.

setup.text: Mark physis/perichondral ring, saphenous structures, fracture zone, plate path, and proximal screw sites; confirm indirect reduction strategy.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark medial malleolus, distal-tibial physis, medial tibial border, greater saphenous vein/nerve, and tibial shaft axis.

incision.text: Start just proximal to physis and extend proximally according to fracture/plate; begin at medial-malleolar tip only when plate must cross physis.

superficial_interval.text: Deepen through subcutaneous fat and retract greater saphenous vein and saphenous nerve anteriorly using a blunt retractor.

deep_interval.text: Avoid periosteal dissection at physis/perichondral ring and advance plate proximally in a submuscular, bone-hugging plane beneath intact injury-zone tissue.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous saphenous plane, preserved perichondral/periosteal layer, submuscular tunnel, then medial tibia.

structures_encountered.text: Greater saphenous vein, saphenous nerve, medial physis/perichondral ring, periosteum, and medial tibia are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Saphenous nerve/vein, distal-tibial physis and perichondral ring, periosteal blood supply, skin over plate, and posterior structures with off-bone tunneling are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not dissect periosteum at physis or injure perichondral ring; keep plate on bone and visualize each percutaneous screw trajectory.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract saphenous structures bluntly anterior and avoid forceful tunneling that perforates skin, strips periosteum, or enters fracture.

exposure.text: Permits submuscular bridge plating while preserving soft tissue and blood supply within metaphyseal injury zone.

limitations.text: Does not directly expose articular comminution and relies on imaging and indirect reduction to prevent malalignment.

extensions.text: Use separate proximal stab incisions for screws or an anterolateral tunnel when medial soft tissue is compromised.

indications.text: Use for selected unstable pediatric distal-tibial metaphyseal or high-energy tibial fractures suited to bridge plating.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose direct reduction for displaced articular/physeal incongruity and another fixation method when plate crosses critical physis unnecessarily or medial skin is unsafe.

implant_implications.text: Choose pediatric-appropriate plate length and contour, minimize physeal crossings, and position screws through targeted incisions away from physis and neurovascular structures.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use full-length AP/lateral and ankle views to verify length, rotation, coronal/sagittal alignment, physis, plate position, and screw containment.

closure.text: Ensure saphenous structures are free and plate is not prominent beneath skin, then close each incision in layers without tension.

complications.text: Complications include physeal injury, malalignment, saphenous neuritis, skin/plate irritation, infection, delayed union/nonunion, and implant removal.

bailouts.text: Add a limited direct-reduction window or change fixation when indirect maneuvers cannot restore acceptable length, rotation, and alignment.

procedure_applications.condition: An unstable metaphyseal fracture requires bridge plating with maximal preservation of the injury-zone biology

questions.question: Which structures are retracted anteriorly?
questions.answer: Greater saphenous vein and saphenous nerve.

questions.question: Which growth structure must not be dissected?
questions.answer: The perichondral ring at distal tibial physis.

questions.question: When does incision begin at malleolar tip?
questions.answer: When fracture configuration requires plate to cross physis.
